brute.name: Repeated Search in Unsorted List
brute.technique: For each number in the array, treat it as a sequence start and repeatedly search for current + 1 in the original list using a while loop.
brute.teaches: Shows how checking for existence in an unsorted list leads to repeated linear scans across the entire array, causing a cubic time explosion (n * n * n).

better.name: Sort and Linear Scan
better.technique: Sort the array first in O(n log n). Then do a single pass comparing adjacent elements: skip duplicates, extend streak if nums[i] == nums[i-1] + 1, or reset streak to 1 if there is a gap.
better.space: O(1) auxiliary (or O(n) depending on sort implementation)
better.teaches: Demonstrates how sorting eliminates searching by grouping consecutive values adjacently, but hits the O(n log n) comparison sorting ceiling, violating the interview's O(n) requirement.

optimal.name: HashSet + Sequence Start Check
optimal.technique: Insert all numbers into a HashSet for O(1) average lookups. For each number x, check if x - 1 exists in the set. If x - 1 exists, x is not a start—skip it immediately. Only if x - 1 is missing, walk forward checking x + 1, x + 2, ... and update max streak.
optimal.teaches: Proves how combining fast O(1) hash lookups with sequence-head detection (pruning redundant mid-sequence starts) guarantees every sequence element is visited only once during forward walks, achieving strictly linear O(n) time.

decision_reasoning.D1_brute_teaches_why: YES — naive list scanning (O(n³)) viscerally exposes why searching an unsorted collection repeatedly is disastrous.
decision_reasoning.D2_better_distinct: YES — sorting (O(n log n)) teaches how adjacent grouping solves search without extra space, but hits the sorting barrier when O(n) is demanded.
decision_reasoning.D4_data_structure_problem: NO — lookup and sequence-head detection algorithmic progression.
decision_reasoning.D5_fewer_is_better: The 3-tier pedagogical progression (Unsorted Scan O(n³) → Sort & Scan O(n log n) → HashSet Sequence Start O(n)) provides the complete journey from naive intuition to sorting trap to optimal linear mastery across 13 scenes.
